item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement `retry_budget.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: repository quality-retry-budget has SPEC.md, retry_budget.py (stub) and test_retry_budget.py (basic tests). Read SPEC.md first; it is the source of truth.

Requirements:
- Keep the exact signature: retry_delay(attempt, elapsed_ms, *, max_attempts=4, budget_ms=1000, base_ms=100, cap_ms=400, retry_after_ms=None) -> int | None.
- Validate ALL arguments before any early return. Numbers must be built-in int (reject bool and float). attempt and max_attempts >= 1; elapsed_ms, budget_ms, base_ms, cap_ms and non-None retry_after_ms >= 0. Raise ValueError on invalid input. No upper limit on ints.
- attempt >= max_attempts -> None (attempt > max_attempts is legal).
- backoff = min(cap_ms, base_ms * 2**(attempt-1)); zero base or zero cap yields zero; saturate without building a huge power of two (e.g. cap the exponent or short-circuit when base_ms is 0 or the shift exceeds the cap's bit length).
- If retry_after_ms supplied: delay = max(backoff, retry_after_ms); the floor is not limited by cap_ms.
- If elapsed_ms + delay >= budget_ms -> None; otherwise return delay (zero allowed). Never shorten the wait.
- Never sleep, read a clock, use randomness, network or third-party packages; do not mutate inputs.

Tests: extend test_retry_budget.py with focused stdlib unittest tests covering every validation error (bool, float, negative, zero attempt, zero max_attempts, each argument), attempt boundary (== and > max_attempts), exponent saturation with huge attempt values, zero base/zero cap, base > cap, retry_after above and below backoff and above cap, budget boundary (exactly equal to budget -> None, one less -> allowed), and zero delay returned. Run the tests and confirm they pass.

Code style: functions under 60 lines, at least two meaningful assertions/validations per non-trivial function at the boundary, no try/except that hides failure, no comments except where non-obvious (max 2 lines each), no abstractions beyond the spec.

Git: commit the work on the local branch with a clear message. Use the existing git identity of the repository only; do not set or override user.name/user.email. Do not push. Do not add any attribution lines mentioning Claude, Anthropic, or generated-by tooling. Do not delegate.
